source_refs.note: Topic 12.11.2, printed page 283. The printed gypsum formula CaSO4.5H2O is marked as a book error (dihydrate).

blocks.text: Sulfur is an essential nutrient for plant growth. When soils become depleted in sulfate, sulfur can be restored in soil by applying sulfur containing N/P fertilizers, or sulfur-coated fertilizers such as sulfur-coated urea. Soil components and microbes convert elemental sulfur into soluble forms for the use of plants. Gypsum (CaSO₄·5H₂O) is also used as a fertilizer.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O, not CaSO₄·5H₂O.
